deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics. It is the title page (wrapper sheet) of the fair copy of Riemann's memoir. It reads: 'Über die Fortpflanzung ebener Luftwellen von endlicher Schwingungsweite. Ein Beitrag zur Theorie der partiellen Differentialgleichungen. v. B. Riemann. Der Königlichen Societät überreicht am 17. Nov. 1859.'

In English: 'On the propagation of plane air waves of finite amplitude. A contribution to the theory of partial differential equations. By B. Riemann. Submitted to the Royal Society [of Sciences, Göttingen] on 17 Nov. 1859.'

The memoir was printed in Abh. Kgl. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen, Bd. 8 (1860). It solves the 1-D compressible Euler equations by characteristics, using what are now called Riemann invariants r, s. It also treats the 'Verdichtungsstoß' (shock) through jump conditions and solves the piecewise-constant initial-value problem now called the Riemann problem.

The subtitle on this sheet differs from the printed title. The printed paper carries only the main title. Its introduction then speaks of 'a contribution to the theory of *non-linear* partial differential equations', the phrasing that also appears in the draft on the next page. So the cover-sheet subtitle is an earlier or shorter form of that framing.

The faint writing across the page is show-through or offset from the other side of the sheet or the facing leaf. It is not new content. Visible fragments match the previous page's shock analysis, e.g. square-root expressions of the type (ρ'−ρ1)(f(ρ')−f(ρ1)) / (ρ1 ρ'). Here f(ρ) plays the role of the pressure in the jump condition. That is the momentum/mass jump condition (Rankine–Hugoniot type, without the energy equation, since Riemann assumes a pressure–density law). No new derivation can be read from it.

results.what: Title page and submission date of the 1859 memoir on plane air waves of finite amplitude (characteristics, Riemann invariants, shocks, Riemann problem)
results.modern_name: Riemann's 1860 paper on gas dynamics: Riemann invariants, method of characteristics, Riemann problem, shock jump conditions

deep.surprise_reason: Pure title page of Riemann's well-known published memoir. The only marginal points of interest are bibliographic: the submission date of 17 Nov. 1859 and the subtitle 'Ein Beitrag zur Theorie der partiellen Differentialgleichungen', which is absent from the printed title. The faint mathematics is show-through of the adjacent shock computations.

checkable.asserts: Context only (show-through from the previous page): for the isothermal law p=a^2*rho, the shock velocity-jump relation (u1-u')^2=(rho'-rho1)(p'-p1)/(rho1 rho') gives |u1-u'|/a = sqrt(rho'/rho1)-sqrt(rho1/rho'), as used on the previous page.

transcription_corrections: The faint, mirror-like formulas over the page are bleed-through from the reverse/facing leaf and should not be transcribed as content of this page.
Subtitle reading 'Ein Beitrag zur Theorie der partiellen Differentialgleichungen' looks correct. Note that 'nicht linearen' does not appear here, unlike the printed introduction.
Possible stray marks at the right edge ('zu S.4', 'zu S.6') belong to the adjacent leaf (the letter with corrections to S. 4 and S. 6), not to this page.
